findings.claim: The tests only inspect files whose names start with "Formatters.". The resolver (GeneratedMessagePackResolver) and any other generated type are never checked. The requirement says all generated code, and the test comment claims every emitted formatter is covered. If the resolver is meant to be in scope, removing or never adding the attribute there would go unnoticed. The change also adds no attribute to the resolver template.

findings.claim: The first test asserts only that each file contains the attribute somewhere and that there are at least 4 files. A file with several formatters (for example nested types) is not checked per class, so deleting the attribute from one template while another formatter in the same file keeps it would survive. The count threshold of 4 is also weak. EnumTemplate, UnionTemplate, StringKey and Formatter may all be covered by separate files, but nothing ties each template to its own file.

findings.claim: The guard condition `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is checked only as a literal string. No test compiles the generated code against a netstandard2.0 or net472 target, or against a modern one, so the requirement that the generated code compiles on every target is unverified. The guard could be mutated to `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` and the second test would still pass if Guard were changed in step. Note that the Guard constant is duplicated in the test rather than derived.
